Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
16 October 2026 .
Brent $ 109.48 + 3.29 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 CBS News and FreightWaves warn ships in the Strait of Hormuz still face indiscriminate attacks, with container vessel strikes escalating.

02 Brent stood at $109.48, up 3.29% over 24 hours, as of 18:15 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 The IEA has agreed to accelerate release of approximately 100 million barrels of emergency oil stocks as the Hormuz crisis drags on, per gCaptain.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains a running hazard for commercial shipping. CBS News and FreightWaves report that maritime monitors are warning vessels in the strait still face indiscriminate attacks, with strikes on container ships continuing to escalate. Separately, Iran's navy claims additional tankers have caught fire east of the strait after entering areas it designates as prohibited; no maritime authority has confirmed those claims. A projectile strike injuring 11 crew members, reported by UA.NEWS citing The Hindu, was reported on October 15; no source in this window gives the date of the attack or names the vessel, and it is separate from the sinking of the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, which remains in the news cycle. Two ships have been reported sunk near the strait following strikes, per WWD and Yahoo, and Singapore-registered vessels have been struck in the strait, per CNBC; Asia Insurance Review notes the attacks raise marine insurance risks. The IEA has agreed to accelerate the release of approximately 100 million barrels of emergency oil stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel, per gCaptain. Iran's Tehran Times, a single source, claims the strait will remain closed until passage is coordinated with Tehran, consistent with the background position; WANA News Agency, also a single source, says it will stay closed until Iran's rights are respected. Brent stood at $109.48, up 3.29% over 24 hours, as of 18:15 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The feed indexed 63 headlines in the last 24 hours. As of 18:22 UTC, 131 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
